- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for early periods.
- If sentiment is positive (1.00) or shows upward momentum, model often underestimates sharp spikes; increase forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 80, forecast tends to drop; if below 70, tends to rise — apply correction based on 30-day moving average divergence.
- Overshoot after spikes: if true outcome shows sharp drop after peak, model overcorrects; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5 days.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to lagging; if sentiment is stable, add 0.5–1.5% lag correction to forecast for next 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows no change (all 0.00), model tends to forecast flat; if true outcome shows volatility, add 1–3% volatility buffer to forecast.
